clinicalPearls: Autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia caused by heterozygous variants in ELOVL4 (elongation of very-long-chain fatty acids protein 4) on chromosome 6q14.
Classically pairs cerebellar ataxia with erythrokeratodermia — figurate hyperkeratotic, papulosquamous skin plaques — as originally described in the French-Canadian Giroux-Barbeau kindred.
Skin lesions may appear in childhood and precede the neurological syndrome by years, and can wax and wane; however, some ELOVL4 ataxia families have no cutaneous involvement.
Neurologically there is adult-onset, slowly progressive gait and limb ataxia with dysarthria and nystagmus.

Allelic disorders are important: different ELOVL4 variants cause autosomal dominant Stargardt-like macular dystrophy, while biallelic variants cause a severe neuro-ichthyosis with spasticity and seizures.
ELOVL4 is essential for synthesis of very-long-chain fatty acids in the epidermal barrier, retina and brain, which explains the cutaneous and retinal associations.
Combined dermatological review with skin biopsy and neurogenetic testing strengthens the diagnosis.
Retinal assessment is worthwhile given the gene's central role in photoreceptor lipid metabolism.
reference.pathophysiology: SCA34 results from heterozygous variants in ELOVL4, which encodes an endoplasmic-reticulum membrane fatty-acid elongase that catalyses a rate-limiting step in the synthesis of very-long-chain fatty acids and related sphingolipids — molecules abundant in the epidermal permeability barrier, retinal photoreceptors and the brain. The dominant ataxia variants are thought to act through a dominant-negative or misfolding mechanism, with mutant protein retained in the endoplasmic reticulum and impairing very-long-chain fatty-acid synthesis in Purkinje neurons and keratinocytes; this shared tissue dependence accounts for the pairing of progressive cerebellar degeneration with erythrokeratodermia. Distinct mutational mechanisms in the same gene underlie the dominant macular dystrophy and the recessive ichthyosis phenotypes, illustrating marked allelic heterogeneity.
additionalDifferentials: Other dominant sibling subtypes with pure or near-pure cerebellar ataxia (for example SCA5, SCA6, SCA14)
SCA7 — dominant ataxia distinguished by pigmentary maculopathy and visual loss
Sjogren-Larsson syndrome — ichthyosis with spastic paraparesis and a lipid-metabolism defect
Erythrokeratodermia variabilis from connexin (GJB) gene defects, without ataxia
Refsum disease and other peroxisomal or lipid-storage ataxias
Biallelic ELOVL4 neuro-ichthyosis — the far more severe recessive counterpart
additionalInvestigations: MRI of the brain to demonstrate cerebellar atrophy
Dermatological assessment with skin biopsy of representative plaques
ELOVL4 sequencing or a hereditary-ataxia gene panel
Ophthalmological and retinal examination to detect macular involvement
Plasma very-long-chain fatty acid and phytanic acid screen to exclude peroxisomal mimics
Genetic counselling and family segregation study
redFlags: Rapidly progressive ataxia or spasticity raising concern for the severe biallelic phenotype
Widespread ichthyosiform erythroderma in an infant, suggesting recessive disease
reference.prognosis: The dominant ataxia is slowly progressive over decades with generally preserved life expectancy, and the associated skin lesions are chronic but not life-threatening; the recessive, biallelic form is by contrast severe and disabling from early life.
pitfalls: Overlooking the skin signs or dismissing them as an unrelated primary dermatosis
Assuming all ELOVL4 disease is identical, when ataxia, macular dystrophy and ichthyosis carry different genotype-phenotype correlations
Missing the diagnosis in the subset of families without any cutaneous features
Neglecting retinal examination and thereby missing coexistent maculopathy
references: Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology
Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: No disease-modifying therapy exists for the ataxia, so centre care on physiotherapy for gait and balance, occupational therapy, and speech and language therapy
Manage the erythrokeratodermia dermatologically with emollients, topical keratolytics and topical or oral retinoids under dermatology
Arrange ophthalmological and retinal surveillance for macular involvement, given the allelic Stargardt-like macular dystrophy
Institute falls prevention and provide mobility aids for gait and limb ataxia
Monitor for bulbar dysfunction with periodic swallow assessment
Coordinate multidisciplinary follow-up across neurology, dermatology and ophthalmology
Offer genetic counselling and cascade testing, counselling that biallelic ELOVL4 variants cause a severe recessive neuro-ichthyosis with spasticity and seizures
